text.english_translation: "Hail! Prosperity! In the year next to the year following the Eighth(3)year of King Saḍaiyan Māran:Kāḍambanaṭṭi, also called Parāntaka Aḍalaiyūr Nāḍalvān(4), endowed sevenmās and seven and a half Kaḷañju of refined gold(5) for a lamp, to be keptalight for ever, for the Mādévar(6) of the Tirumūlattānam(7) in Tirunalak-kuṇram of Kuṇriyūr nāḍu. May this be protected by the residents ofPunnaṅguḍi(8) and Parambaiyūr.(9) Let their feet be for ever on my head.In the tenth year of the king: Nākan Kaḍi..........................................ofNenmalai nāḍu endowed...........mā and one kaḷañju of gold to the Perumā-ṇadikal for a seven day festival."(1) This is in accordance with Prof. K. A. N. Sastry's chronology. The period corresponds tothat between the close of the 6th century A. D. and the beginning of the 10th century, and denotesthe Pāṇḍya line which was contemporary with the Pallavas, till its extinction by Vijayālaya, thefounder of the Cōla Empire.(2) Unidentified in the 'Chronological List of Inscriptions'. This inscription is attributed toJatila-Kōccadaiyan Raṇadhīra (C. 710-740 A.D.) in the Revised Manual of the Pudukkoṭṭai State(Vol. II, i, p. 553), where he is called Saḍaiyan Māran. He must have been a Māran Saḍaiyan andthe palaeography of this record does not warrant such an early date. The name of the donor, achief who bore the name of Parāntaka, affords some clue to the identification. The name wasborne by two early Pāṇḍiya Kings, Jatila Parāntaka Neḍuñjaḍaiyan Varaguṇa Mahārāja (C. 765-815A. D.) who preceded Śrī Māra Śrī Vallabha, and Parāntaka Vīranārāyaṇa (C. 880-900) who was thesecond in succession from Śrī Māra. The Pāṇḍiyas cannot have been in possession ofthis territory in the second half of the 9th century since the Pallava Nrpatuṅga's reign (849-875 A.D.)extended over these parts-we have a record of his 7th year in Nārttāmalai (P. S. I. 18)-and theCōla Parakēsari Vijayālaya rose to power, conquered Tanjore and established the foundations of theCōla Empire about 850 A. D. We have to look for a date in the first half of the century, when thehold of the Pallavas on these parts was precarious, when the authority of the Muttaraiyar, the Pallavasubordinates who ruled over these parts, was weak and the Pāṇḍyas had conquered part of the countrybeyond the Kāvēri driving back the Pallava armies, though only for a brief time. This would bethe time of Jatila Parāntaka, Māran Saḍaiyan (C. 765-815) and that of his successor Śrī Māra ŚrīVallabha, Saḍaiyan Māran (815-862). We have three records of the former (P. S. I. 239-41), and thisrecord is to be attributed to Śrī Māra, since it is dated in the time of Saḍaiyan Māran. The chief,the donor in this record, perhaps served under both the former, whose name he adopted, andthe latter. As has been noted in foot-note 1, under P. S. I. 287, there are no records of the PallavaDantivarman (775-826 A. D.) dated between his 17th and 51st years in the Cōla country, whereas onefinds many Pāṇḍiya inscriptions of this period as far north as South Arcot. The Pāṇḍiyas musthave gained these territories, just after the decline of the power of Ilaṅgō Muttaraiyar, who assertedhis independence briefly during the earlier part of this period, as P. S. I. 287, shows. This Śrī MāraŚrī Vallabha is the same as Avanipasēkhara Śrī Vallabha in the unpublished inscription on the rockto the south of the Jain cave-temple in Sittannavāśal.(3) This is the date given in the supplementary part of the inscription.(4) The date in the first line is lost and reads................+1st year+1st year. This system ofdating is usual in Pāṇḍiya inscriptions. Probably the first number (which is lost here) denotes theregnal year of the king in which some important event took place, and from which later dates werereckoned by addition.(5) Evidently the chief bore the name of Parāntaka Māran Saḍaiyan. See above.(6) Tuḷaippon.(7) Mahādēvar.(8) Mūlasthānam or sanctum.(9) Modern Pinnaṅguḍi village.(10) Modern Parambūr village.

cells.location: Alangudi Taluk, Tirugokarnam, in the Gokarnesvara temple, on the south wall of the Variver temple
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 15 paṇam (= 15 kaḻañju of gold) for maintaining and ever burning lamp (nontī-viḷakku) in the temple at Gōkarṇam (in) Tiruvelpūr by Varaguṇamātāriyār, alias Nakkanētti of Kalkālchēri, a kaṟippal of Vaḷa-nāḍu.

16. வெத்த பொன்

cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the 17th year of the King Maranjadaiyan, I,
Nakkanicetti, also called Varagunavati Araiyan*, of Kalkuricci in Kavirpal*
of Vallanadu, endowed 15 pon--fifteen kalanjus* of gold, which I collected
by begging*, for a lamp to be kept alight for ever for the Madevar* of
Gokarnam in Tiruvelpur*. This gold was placed under the protection of
the nattar*."

cells.tamil_fields: header_tamil: மேற்கண்ட 238-ஈ. சாசனத்தில் கூறிய கோயிலின் வடக்குபுறம்தான் கீழ்முகத்துத்துள்ள சாசனம்,—
cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the twenty-third year of King Maranjadaiyan.........
..................endowment of....................refined gold* for a lamp to be kept
alight for ever*, for the Perumanadikal* of the Tirumulattanam* in
Tirunalakkunram......................"

Footnotes:
[Footnote 1] Unidentified in the 'Chronological List of Inscriptions'. See Prof. K. A. N. Sastri, 'The
Pandyan Kingdom' (1929), pp. 40-41, et seqq. His Anaimalai record (A. R. E. 454 of 1906) is dated in
the year 3871 (expired) of the Kaliyuga era which corresponds to 770 A. D. "We thus get a definite
date in the reign of Parantaka I Varaguna Maharaja "......" His inscriptions range from the third
regnal year (Velvikkudi grant) to the forty-third (605 of 1915 from Eravadi) and it may well be that
he reigned for fifty years, say 765-815 A. D.". Mr. Gopinath Rao, who edited the Trivandrum Museum
inscription of Maran-jadaiyan, assigns him to the second half of the 8th century. The present
inscription is ascribed to this king from the name Maranjadaiyan, which is further confirmed by the
name of the donor--Varagunavati (Varagunapati) Araiyan, borne-after one of the titles of the king.
The king could not have been Maran Sadaiyan Varagunavarman II (C. 862-880 A. D.) since
Ilango Muttaraiyar (See P. S. I. 237) had become independent and powerful in this region in the
earlier half of the century, the Cola Vijayalaya had come to power after defeating the Muttaraiyars
and Pallavas by about 850 A. D. and this Pandiya cannot have left three records, P. S. I. 239-41
ranging from the 17th to 23rd years in this part of the country.
[Footnote 2] Varagunapati.
[Footnote 3] Kalkuricci or Karkuricci was the old name of Tirukkattalai.
[Footnote 4] Kavirpal--the district called 'Kavir'.
[Footnote 5] The pon and kalanju are equated. Pon perhaps refers to a minted coin, while kalanju is the
customary gold weight.
[Footnote 6] Unnattu probably derived from unni-attudal. Unnudal--to collect by begging for a holy
purpose. This custom of making a vow to collect money or rice by begging for offerings to a God,
with a view to humble oneself, prevails among Hindus of South India even at present.
[Footnote 7] Mahadevar.
[Footnote 8] Modern Tiruvappur.
[Footnote 9] Nattar--the local administrative body of the Nadu or district.
[Footnote 10] Unidentified in the 'Chronological List of Inscriptions'. See foot-note 1 under P. S. I. 289.
[Footnote 11] Tujaippon.
[Footnote 12] Tiru-nonda-vilakku.
[Footnote 13] The Lord--Siva.
[Footnote 14] Tirumulasthanam--refers to the sanctum of the Melaikkovil.

cells.tamil_fields: header_tamil: திருமய்யம் தாலுகா, பெருந்துறை, சிவன்கோவிலில் ஸ்வாமிகோவிலின் தெற்கு முன் மண்டபத்து தென்புறம் பட்டியிலுள்ள சாசனம்,—
cells.inscription_text:
1. ஸ்ரீஸ்ரீ [*] கொச்செடைபன்மாராக ஸ்ரீ சுந்தரச[ச்]ழ பாண்டியதெவற்கு
யாண்டு ஙஉ டாவது இராஜ இராஜப் பாண்டி நாட்..
2. ஜெகவீரசொழவளநாட்டுக்காரணாட்டுப்பெருந்துறை . . . 5 . . . கொண்மாவாகென்
சுந்தரசொழபாண்டிய சுவராமமுதலர்ற் . . . .
3. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . க்கரைமாசாணி . . . . .
[அ]ரைக்காணி நரிப்பனகாடு காணி அரைக்காணி¹
4. ன்தான் இரண்சொமாக்கணி முந்திரிகை சொடி . டியி பெ .
புற[க்]ரை வட்டம் காணியும் ஆக இந்நிலத்² . . . . .
5. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . இழப்பதானோம் நீர்வார்த்து குடுத்தோம் [*]
cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the 12th year of Śrī Sundara Cōla-Pāṇḍiya Dēvar,
also called Kōccadaiyapanmar, (1) I, Kōnmāyan of Perundurai in
Kāṉanāḍu (2) of Rājēndracōḷavaḷanāḍu (3) in Rājarājap-pāṇḍiṉāḍu (4), made the
following endowment of lands to the Lord who abides in Sundara-
cōḷīśvaram (5) .................................... lands measuring araimākkāṇi (6),
........................ lands measuring araikkāṇi (7), Naripaṇaṅgāḍu lands
measuring kāni-araikkāṇi (8), .................................ntaran lands measuring
two mākkāṇi-muntirikai (9), Cōla-pāṇḍiya (purum?) purakarai vaṭṭam lands
measuring one kāni (10). Thus, agreeing to pay (all the taxes on these
lands) myself, I gave these lands with due oblations of water."

cells.location: Mel. T. taluk, Kottaiyur, in the Amalieevar temple, inscription on the south wall of the Swami temple,—
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Begins with the historical introduction of the king commencing with the words Pugala-mādu [puva-lōka ...] . Seems to record a royal order granting tax-free dēvadāna (...) land to the temple of Tirumagutti-Īsvara[m]-uḍaiya-Mahādēva of Kōṭṇiyūr in Kōna-nāḍu. It is said that the king Śrīvallabhadeva issued the above order when he was pleased to take his seat on the throne (Palli-kattil) called Pāṇḍya-tōjan in the hall Alaṅgā[ya]-Pāṇḍiyan, within the inner apartments of his palace at Madurai.

"Hail! Prosperity! When Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ Śrī Vallabha Dēvar,
also called Kōccadaípanmar (3), the pre-eminent King (4) who revived the
splendour of the line of the Moon, which dated from the beginnings of
creation (5), on whose majestic shoulders the Goddess of Prosperity and the

(1) See foot-note 1 above.
(2) District.
(3) Province.
(4) Territorial Division.
(5) Evidently the temple was named after the viceroy.
(6) 9/160 (of a vēli).
(7) 1/160 (of a vēli).
(8) 3/160 (of a vēli).
(9) 1/10+1/64 (of a vēli).
(10) 1/30 (of a vēli).
* This is in accordance with the chronology of Prof. K. A. N. Sastry. This period begins from
the end of the Cōla-Vijayalaya line and the beginning of the Cōla-Cālukya line with Kulōttuṅga
Cōla I, (1070 A. D.) and lasted till and sometime after the Muhammadan invasion of South India and
their occupation of Madura, i. e. till about the 15th century.
1 A. R. E. 21 of 1917 of the 10th year of Jaṭāvarman Śrī Vallabha mentions the 31st year of
Kulōttuṅga who took Kollam, doubtless Kulōttuṅga I. "Śrī Vallabha's 10th year is later than the
31st year of Kulōttuṅga I, i. e., 1101, so that Śrī Vallabha's rule did not begin earlier than 1091 A.D."
See Prof. K. A. N. Sastry, 'The Pāṇḍyan Kingdom' p.p. 118-19, p. 119 note and 120-22, 'Cōlas' II,ii,
p. 21 and note.
2 For a comparison of the texts of the praśasti see S. I., L., V, p. 108; no. 294; and p. 111, no. 298.
3 Kō-Sadaiya-panmar-King Jaṭāvarman.
4 Kō-mudal.
5 Mā-mudal-maḍī-k-kulam-viḷakkiya.


Goddess of Victory were pleased to abide¹, by whom the vast Kingdom
attained great fame², who brought the territory in the eight directions
under the shade of his parasol³, at whose feet all the kings came and paid
homage ⁴, who put on the hereditary crown that was set with jewels 10 and
was enthroned in all majesty along with Ulakamuḷududaiyāḷ, his queen, on
the exalted Virasiṁhāsanam, while the authority of the Kayal extended
along with the growing power of his sceptre over the great territory which
had as its only boundaries the bellowing seas extending (on both sides) from
Ten-kumari¹¹, was pleased to sit on the Pāṇḍiyarājan 12 in the Alagiya-
pāṇḍiyan Hall, in the inner apartments¹³ of the Palace¹⁴ in Madurai, was
pleased to issue the following commands, to be executed by the puravari-
tiṇai-k-kaḷattār 15.

Whereas, (we have been informed) that there has been no assignment, in
former times, of dévadāna-iraiyili 16 lands to the Mahādēva 17 who abides
in Tiruvagattīsvaram temple 18 in Kōttaiyūr of Kānaṉādu, and that in
order to provide for the needs of service of this Dēvar...............................
lands in the waterspread of the tank in this village...................................

text.english_translation: "Hail! Prosperity! When Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ Śrī Vallabha Dēvar,also called Kōccadaípanmar (3), the pre-eminent King (4) who revived thesplendour of the line of the Moon, which dated from the beginnings ofcreation (5), on whose majestic shoulders the Goddess of Prosperity and the(1) See foot-note 1 above.(2) District.(3) Province.(4) Territorial Division.(5) Evidently the temple was named after the viceroy.(6) 9/160 (of a vēli).(7) 1/160 (of a vēli).(8) 3/160 (of a vēli).(9) 1/10+1/64 (of a vēli).(10) 1/30 (of a vēli).* This is in accordance with the chronology of Prof. K. A. N. Sastry. This period begins fromthe end of the Cōla-Vijayalaya line and the beginning of the Cōla-Cālukya line with KulōttuṅgaCōla I, (1070 A. D.) and lasted till and sometime after the Muhammadan invasion of South India andtheir occupation of Madura, i. e. till about the 15th century.1 A. R. E. 21 of 1917 of the 10th year of Jaṭāvarman Śrī Vallabha mentions the 31st year ofKulōttuṅga who took Kollam, doubtless Kulōttuṅga I. "Śrī Vallabha's 10th year is later than the31st year of Kulōttuṅga I, i. e., 1101, so that Śrī Vallabha's rule did not begin earlier than 1091 A.D."See Prof. K. A. N. Sastry, 'The Pāṇḍyan Kingdom' p.p. 118-19, p. 119 note and 120-22, 'Cōlas' II,ii,p. 21 and note.2 For a comparison of the texts of the praśasti see S. I., L., V, p. 108; no. 294; and p. 111, no. 298.3 Kō-Sadaiya-panmar-King Jaṭāvarman.4 Kō-mudal.5 Mā-mudal-maḍī-k-kulam-viḷakkiya.Goddess of Victory were pleased to abide¹, by whom the vast Kingdomattained great fame², who brought the territory in the eight directionsunder the shade of his parasol³, at whose feet all the kings came and paidhomage ⁴, who put on the hereditary crown that was set with jewels 10 andwas enthroned in all majesty along with Ulakamuḷududaiyāḷ, his queen, onthe exalted Virasiṁhāsanam, while the authority of the Kayal extendedalong with the growing power of his sceptre over the great territory whichhad as its only boundaries the bellowing seas extending (on both sides) fromTen-kumari¹¹, was pleased to sit on the Pāṇḍiyarājan 12 in the Alagiya-pāṇḍiyan Hall, in the inner apartments¹³ of the Palace¹⁴ in Madurai, waspleased to issue the following commands, to be executed by the puravari-tiṇai-k-kaḷattār 15.Whereas, (we have been informed) that there has been no assignment, informer times, of dévadāna-iraiyili 16 lands to the Mahādēva 17 who abidesin Tiruvagattīsvaram temple 18 in Kōttaiyūr of Kānaṉādu, and that inorder to provide for the needs of service of this Dēvar...............................lands in the waterspread of the tank in this village...................................

cells.inscription_text:
1. ஸ்வஸ்தி ஸ்ரீ [[1*]] ஸ்ரீ^^ஹனச்ச்ருவதிகள் ஸ்ரீகுலசெவற்[தி]வற்கு

மட்டியுநிற்மிட[ர]கை [மு]த்தார்க்கெம்பரி3

"Hail! Prosperity! In the 9th year of Tribhuvanaccakravartīkal Śrī
Kulaśēkhara Dēvar, I. Kēraḷan Niṣadharājan, also called Tirukkoḍuṅkuṇramudaiyān³, of Ponnamarāvati in Puramaḷaināḍu, gave as a pious⁴ gift
to Mutṭa Bhaṭṭa Sōmayāji of Prayāgai⁵ (?) the following lands:-the lands
called Mutṭarnēmpari...,⁹ in the eastern hamlet⁷ of Maṭṭiyūr. The boun-
daries of these lands are:-the eastern boundary to the west of the śevvai (8)*
that runs straight south in the Sēndamaṅgalam vayal and to the extreme
ِlimits of Parpanāpan nemmaiº to a point north of its western end, and lying
to its west; and to the west of the śevvai that extends north to south as
the eastern boundary of Ve...tumēdu in... ... ... ... ... ... ...po...; the southern
boundary to the north of ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...; the western boundary
to the east of the śevvai, that runs north from the boundary of... ... ... ...
... ... ...; and the northern boundary to the south of...... ... ... ... ... ...the
entire tank bund (10) of Sēndamaṅgalam. I hereby gave to this Prayāgai
Bhaṭṭa Sōmayāji, with libations of water, the whole tank and all the
smaller tanks, 10 wet lands, dry lands, trees, wells, and everything else
within the boundaries thus specified, after exempting it from all kinds of
taxes, with all the rights of possession for so long as the moon and sun
endure, and inscribed this on stone. For his enjoyment of the abovesaid
he shall pay annually as... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...
at the rate of... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... per year. He shall not be
bound to pay anything else. I, the said Niṣadharājan... ... ... ... ...
inscribed this on stone in favour of the Adi-can-dēśvara. (11) May this be
under the protection of all Mahēśvaras."

லைக்கப்பட்ட நிலத்திற்காட[ு]*மெய —
6. ந்தாராயம் வெட்டிமுட்டி எச்சொறு கூற்றூசி ஓலசிலெ அநைசர்ல[*]-
சல்லரி பெருவரி இதுவாரால் மற்றும் எப்பே-
7. ரப்பட்டவங்குரித்தென் உடெயார் ர[ஜ]*ஜெந்திரசொளியை[மு]டுடைய
நா[ய]னார் கொயிற்றிருக்கமாக்கொட்டலு —
8. டெய ஆஞ[டு]டையாய்ச்சியர்க்குச்சியிருப்படிமாற்றுள்ளிட்டு வெண்டும்
தித்தநிவந்தங்[க]ளுக்கு திருக்கொடுங்குன்றமுடையான்
9. கொனனான விஷல[நா]ததெவன் [[*]] இங்காச்சியர்க்கு இ[ச்]*நாட்டு சிறு-
வயல் புஞ்சை நஞ்சை அகப்பட பெருநிககெல்லையும்
10. திருநாமத்துதால் திருநாமத்துகாணி ஆககத்துருக்கைமலைவிலெ நாவாத்து2

cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the tenth year after the expiry of the thirteenth
year (1) of Kō-Śadaiyappanar (2), also called Tribhuvanacakravartikaḷ Śrī
Kulasekhara Dēvar, I, Niṣadharājan, also called Tirukkoṇuṇram-
uḍaiyān Kēraḷan (3), of Ponnamarāpati, in Puramalaināḍu, in order to
provide for the day-to-day needs of the service, including daily offerings of
rice (4), to the Āluḍaiya Nācciyār, who abides in the Tirukkāmakkōṭṭam (5) in the
temple of the Lord of Rājēndracōliśvaram of this place, gave the rights of
enjoying the kaḍamai, antarāyam, veṭṭi-muṭṭi, eccōru, kūrrarisi, elavai,
araiśarvāśalvari (6), and everything else of the kind, collected from
the lands included within the four boundaries of Malaiyadhvajacaturvēdi-
maṅgalam, also called Veṭkūr. I, Niṣadharājan, also called Tirukkoṇuṇ-
kuṇramuḍaiyān Kēraḷan, made this gift to Āluḍaiya Nācciyār who abides
in the Tirukkāmakkōṭṭam in the temple of the Lord of Rājēndracōliśvaram,
as provision for all the needs of the daily service including offerings of rice.

To the same Nācciyār, I, Kēraḷan Niṣadharājan, hereby gave, with libations
of water on Her sacred hands (7), Siruvayal with all the wet-lands and dry
lands included in its four boundaries, to be tirunāmattukkāṇi (8) and to be
assigned to Her sacred name. (9) May this be under the protection of all
Mahēśvaras ".

Footnotes:
[Footnote 1] Identified as Jaṭāvarman Kulaśēkhara I. though the distinguishing epithet 'Kōccadaiyapaṇmar'
(King Jaṭāvarman) is absent. The chief Tirukkoḍuṅkuṇramudaiyān Kēraḷan Niṣadharājan, who
is the donor here, figures in P. S. I. 161 from Idaiyāṭṭūr dated in the 29th year, of Kulōttuṅga
Cōla III, i. e., 1206-07 A. D. This, and the fact that in is dated in the 9th year, rule out the
possibility of the King being identified as Kulaśēkhara of the Pāṇḍiyan civil war (1108-70 A. D.),
whose accession is dated about 1162 A. D., and who was succeeded by his son Vikrama Pāṇḍiya in
C. 1180.
[Footnote 2] See Prof. K. A. N. Sastry 'The Pāṇḍyan Kingdom' p. 144.
[Footnote 3] Kēraḷan Niṣadharājan, Lord of Pirāmmalai (Tirukkoḍuṅkuṇram).
[Footnote 4] Dharma-dānam.
[Footnote 5] Mutṭa Bhaṭṭa Sōmayāji of Prayāgai-Bhaṭṭa is the title of Brahmins; Sōmayāji is one who
has performed the Sōma sacrifice; Prayāgai is the name of the confluence of the Jumma and Ganges
in Allahabad.
[Footnote 6] Perhaps Mutṭarnēmparikāl.
[Footnote 7] Piḍākai.
[Footnote 8] Sevvai-bund or channel or cultivated land?
[Footnote 9] Padmanābhan.
[Footnote 10] Embal-kaḷum.
[Footnote 11] Probably the lands in question were temple lands bought by the chief to be given as a gift to
the Brahmins.

text.location: Same Taluk, Ponnamarapati, in the Vonesayakovil, on the north prakara wall, the inscription opposite to the Chandisvara deity,—
text.remarks: Records a gift of certain land and also the taxes, viz., kaṇakkāṟyam, eṭṭuprāmāṇ[ik]kāṟyam, durai, araikesēritiravi, peṇvāri, arising from the village of Ve[t]kūr, alias Mahāvidyāchaturvēdimangalam in Puranaikāri-nāḍu, for the daily offerings to Tirakkōḷakuṇḍōruḍaiyān-Alagāya-Nāchchiyār of the temple of Rājēndra-sōliśvaramuḍaiyār. The donor was Tirukkōḷakuṇḍūr-uḍaiyān Kerala[ṅg]ati Niśadanḍarājan of Poṇmaṇṇārpāḍi.

cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the 3rd year² of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ Śrī
Kulaśēkhara Dēvar in whose bosom the Goddess of the lotus flower sat
enthroned,³ with whom the Goddess of the earth was rightfully united⁴;
on whose victorious shoulders the mighty Goddess of victory abode⁵; on
whose tongue the great Goddess of learning abode in all splendour⁶; whose
prowess, like the moon, shone in the eight directions⁷; who, while the gospel
of the Vēdas was strictly observed and the Code of Manu prevailed⁸,
the six forms of religion of established greatness prospered⁹, the
ensign of the tiger along with the ensign of the bow stood permanently
furled up and the beautiful ensign of the carp, planted firmly on the top of
the golden hill, stayed unfurled for ever¹⁰, with his white parasol sheltered
the entire world which rose on the seven seas and was surrounded by the
eight mountains, while the authority of the sceptre of righteousness pre-
vailed so that the cruel Kalī-misery, strife and famine-hid itself in terror
in the deep netherworld¹¹, the Villavar, the Sembiyar, the Virāḷar, the
Marāṭar, and the Pallavar, brought their tributes and paid homage in proper



































order(12), the sole authority of a single discus prevailed over the wide earth(13),
and learning in the three branches of Tamil, which was as sweet as
nectar, namely iyal, isai, and nāṭakam, flourished(14), was seated enthroned
in all majesty on the virasimhāsanam as Kōceṅdaiyanparmar :—(15)
We hereby annul, from this year onwards, the kadamai(16), vari(17) and
antarāyam(18) due from the Pāṇilam-parṟu lands in Tiruvodikālai(19), which
are dēvadānam lands and form part of the dēvadānam holdings of the
Śrī Varamudaiya Nāyanār of Kānanaḍu in Virudhārajābhayankaravalai-
nāḍu, also called Kānanaḍu. I, Kalvāyil Nāḍalvān(20), having enjoined
that this shall continue for so long as the moon and sun endure, had this
gift inscribed on stone."

Footnotes:
[Footnote 1] The text has 'paḍimūnṟāvadin-edir-paṭṭām-āṇḍu' This kind of reckoning is usual in
Pāṇḍiya inscriptions. Probably the first figure signifies the year in which some important event
took place, and from which the dates are reckoned.
[Footnote 2] King Jaṭāvarman Kulasekhara I - See footnote 1 under Inscription 244.
[Footnote 3] Kēraḷan Niṣadharājan, Lord of Tirukkoḍuṅkuṇram (Pirāṇmalai).
[Footnote 4] Tiruppaḍimārru - uṇṭiṟṟu - vēndum - nitta - nivandaṅalukku.
[Footnote 5] Tirukkāmakkōṭṭam - The name for the separate shrine of the Goddess (Amman) in the temple.
[Footnote 6] Kaḍamai - Government land tax; antarāyam, tax payable to the local body; veṭṭi, free food for
labourers on public works, muṭṭi or muṭṭāvuḍai supply of free labour for similar purposes, eccōru or
ercoru, the rice to be given to the village artisans; kūrrarisi, probably the same as arisikkāṇam,
the cess on rice husked from paddy; elavai or ēlvai, a tax levied by the nāḍu, water cess or tax on
surplus yield (?); araiśar-vāśal-vari, the tax payable to the 'king's treasury (araśar-vāśal), peruvari,
major cesses as opposed to śilvari.
[Footnote 7] Tirukkaimālsilē - nirvāttuk - koḍuttēn.
[Footnote 8] Tirunāmattukkāṇi - Kind of free-tenure denoting lands registered in the name of the deity.
[Footnote 9] Tirunāmattāl.
[Footnote 1] This is one of the three forms of the praśasti. The text is published in S. I. I., V, pp. 116-17,
No. 302 (A. R. E. 14 of 1894). A. R. E. 338 of 1916 with the same praśasti is a grant giving
astronomical details. The praśasti in this Inscription is full of mistakes and omissions and has been
restored by comparison with No. 302 of S. I. I., V, pp. 116-17. The other forms of the praśasti
of the King begin with "pū-tala-maṇandai" and "pū-tala-vaniṇai".
[Footnote 2] The reading in the "Inscriptions (Texts) of the Pudukkkōṭṭai State". I, 20, is "pūvir ki-la-ti"
which means the 3rd year. The 'Chronological List of Inscriptions of the Pudukkkōṭṭai State', p. 31,
gives the year as '30'. This is a mistake as the year is too high for this King who is known to
have ruled for 27-28 years.
[Footnote 3] The text reads 'pūvin-kilatti-mey-viriruppa' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'pūvin-kilatti-mēni-
viriruppa'.
[Footnote 4] The text reads 'mēdi-ni-(la)-mādu-nixi-yivapuna' where the (la) is superfluous and what
follows is unintelligible. S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'mēdani-madu-nidiyiṇ-punara' which is clear.
[Footnote 5] The text reads 'viya-pōr-maṇandai-śeyar-puya-t-turuppa' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'vayap-
pōr-maṇandai-jaya-p-puyat-tiruppa'.
[Footnote 6] The text reads 'makkalai-maṇandai-vākkinil (ni)vilanga' white S. I. I., V, No. 302, has
'makkalai-maṇandai-vākkiniḷ-viḷanga.'
[Footnote 7] The text reads 'tikkiruṇandungum-viśai-nīl-verippa' while S. I. I., V, No. 302, has 'tiśai-yiru-
nāṅkum-iśai-nilā-verippa'.
[Footnote 8] The text reads 'manu-nēri-nikaḷa' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has, 'maraṇ-nēri-vaḷara-manu-nēri-
tikala.
[Footnote 9] The text reads 'aru-nanṟa-samayaṅgaḷ-arul-tamaippa' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'aru-neric-
camayaṅgaḷ-ārum-taḷavappa'. The six forms of religion are Śaivam, Vaiṣṇavam, Sāktaim, Sōuram,
Gānapatyam, and Kaumāram, viz., worship of Śiva, Viṣṇu, Śakti, Sūrya, Gaṇapati and Kumāra or
Subrahmanya.
[Footnote 10] The text has 'kāṇal-vēṅgai-villudan-nuḍandu-ninṇa-vara-aṅkaḷ-ākkaśaṇḍai-virriruppa' while
S. I. I., V. No. 302, has 'kāṇa-vēṅgai-viḷudan-urandu-minṇa-kanakaśālattu-virriruppa'. The tiger
was the ensign of the Cōlas, the bow of the Cēras, and the double carp (Kayal-fish) that of the Pāṇḍiyas.
This refers to the ascendancy of the Pāṇḍiyas of the Second Empire, over the Cōlas and Cēras.
[Footnote 11] The text reads 'engr-kēśu (en-giri-sūj)-eḷu-kaḍal-ēlu-poil-venkuḍai-nilarra-śeṅgol-naḍappa
koḍuṅgali-naḍuṅgi-nedum-bilan-kaḷippa' while S. I. I., V, No. 302, has 'en-giri-sūlnda-elu-kaḍal-eḷu-
poil-venkudai-nilarra-irungal-noḍappa-koḍungali-nadungi-nedumbilama-tolippa.'

text.location: Same Taluk, Malaiyakovil, in the Kudapokakovil, on the wall to the right of the entrance, the inscription,—
text.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction of the king commencing with the words பூவன்னி வளருந் திருநெடுமாமகள். Registers the annulment of taxes arising from the devadāna lands of Srivallabhachāriyan-Nāyanār of Kannūr in Kānā-nādu, alias Virudarājabhayankara-vāḻnādu, [at] Nādā[v]ān.
text.tamil_fields: header_tamil: மேற்படி தாலுகா, மலையக்கோவில், குடபோககோவிலின் வாசற்படிக்கு வலது- புறம் சுவரிலுள்ள சாசனம்,—
text.inscription_text: 1. [ஹூ]ஸ்ரீ [[*]] பூனின்கிழத்திமெய்விற்றி-2. ருப்ப மெதிகிலமாது நிதியிவு நா-3. வியத பொர்மமண்டை செயம்பு[ய]*த்தி-4. குப்ப மாக்களைமடந்தை வாக்கிசி-5. (சி)ல் விளங்க திக்கிருந்குங் விசை-6. கின வெறிபடம் மதுரைநகழ் நகழ அநுசு-7. ன்ற சமையங்கள் ஆறுத்தமைப் பு கா-8. கில் வெங்க்கை வினனுடந்துடந்து கிந்-9. நவா அங்களா காசளதந்தை விற்றியு-10. ப்ப எங்கிசு எழுதுக எழெழு பொழி வெ-11. ங்கு கிழற்ற செங்*[க]கொல் நடப்ப கொடு-12. ங்கலி நங்கி நெடுமிலங் கொழிப்ப13. வி லர் செம்பியர் வில்லவை ஆடலர் பல்லமர்14. திரை உறடன் முறைமுறை பபிய இருசெ.15. மிந் ஆளவம ஒரு கெதி ஒவ்[க]* இங்கமுதனாதி16. ப இல விசை நாடம மகிழ்வள்ளர மணி அ-1. Read கொலானை.2. Read நீர் வார்த்து.13717 னி விசயாலயகாதேஷிதருருழிய கொச்ச18 டயபற்மாசு அளவகக்கரகமதிகள்19 (திநிபுணசக்கரவத்திகள்) விசி குலசேகரதெ20 வற்க்கு பாண்டு கூ ஆவது கானகாட[ந*]க்கு விருத21 ராஜபயங்கரவளநாட்டு காசுநாட்டு திரு-22 வொதிகல்லில் காசநாட்டு ஸ்ரீவரமுதப-23 ஙயக்கள தேவதானம் பாணிதம் பற்றிப்24 உள்ள தேவதர்[ன*]ம் உள்ள நிலத்தில் க25 டமையும் வரியும் அந்தராயம் இலா-26 ண்கேமுதல் தனித்தொம [[*] சந்திர[ச*]தி27 த்தவரை செய்வதாக செய்து குடு28 த்தேன் கல்வெட்டி குடுத்தெ29 ன் கல்லில் நாடாம்[வ*]ங்கென் [[*]
text.english_translation: "Hail! Prosperity! In the 3rd year² of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ ŚrīKulaśēkhara Dēvar in whose bosom the Goddess of the lotus flower satenthroned,³ with whom the Goddess of the earth was rightfully united⁴;on whose victorious shoulders the mighty Goddess of victory abode⁵; onwhose tongue the great Goddess of learning abode in all splendour⁶; whoseprowess, like the moon, shone in the eight directions⁷; who, while the gospelof the Vēdas was strictly observed and the Code of Manu prevailed⁸,the six forms of religion of established greatness prospered⁹, theensign of the tiger along with the ensign of the bow stood permanentlyfurled up and the beautiful ensign of the carp, planted firmly on the top ofthe golden hill, stayed unfurled for ever¹⁰, with his white parasol shelteredthe entire world which rose on the seven seas and was surrounded by theeight mountains, while the authority of the sceptre of righteousness pre-vailed so that the cruel Kalī-misery, strife and famine-hid itself in terrorin the deep netherworld¹¹, the Villavar, the Sembiyar, the Virāḷar, theMarāṭar, and the Pallavar, brought their tributes and paid homage in properorder(12), the sole authority of a single discus prevailed over the wide earth(13),and learning in the three branches of Tamil, which was as sweet asnectar, namely iyal, isai, and nāṭakam, flourished(14), was seated enthronedin all majesty on the virasimhāsanam as Kōceṅdaiyanparmar :—(15)We hereby annul, from this year onwards, the kadamai(16), vari(17) andantarāyam(18) due from the Pāṇilam-parṟu lands in Tiruvodikālai(19), whichare dēvadānam lands and form part of the dēvadānam holdings of theŚrī Varamudaiya Nāyanār of Kānanaḍu in Virudhārajābhayankaravalai-nāḍu, also called Kānanaḍu. I, Kalvāyil Nāḍalvān(20), having enjoinedthat this shall continue for so long as the moon and sun endure, had thisgift inscribed on stone."Footnotes:[Footnote 1] The text has 'paḍimūnṟāvadin-edir-paṭṭām-āṇḍu' This kind of reckoning is usual inPāṇḍiya inscriptions. Probably the first figure signifies the year in which some important eventtook place, and from which the dates are reckoned.[Footnote 2] King Jaṭāvarman Kulasekhara I - See footnote 1 under Inscription 244.[Footnote 3] Kēraḷan Niṣadharājan, Lord of Tirukkoḍuṅkuṇram (Pirāṇmalai).[Footnote 4] Tiruppaḍimārru - uṇṭiṟṟu - vēndum - nitta - nivandaṅalukku.[Footnote 5] Tirukkāmakkōṭṭam - The name for the separate shrine of the Goddess (Amman) in the temple.[Footnote 6] Kaḍamai - Government land tax; antarāyam, tax payable to the local body; veṭṭi, free food forlabourers on public works, muṭṭi or muṭṭāvuḍai supply of free labour for similar purposes, eccōru orercoru, the rice to be given to the village artisans; kūrrarisi, probably the same as arisikkāṇam,the cess on rice husked from paddy; elavai or ēlvai, a tax levied by the nāḍu, water cess or tax onsurplus yield (?); araiśar-vāśal-vari, the tax payable to the 'king's treasury (araśar-vāśal), peruvari,major cesses as opposed to śilvari.[Footnote 7] Tirukkaimālsilē - nirvāttuk - koḍuttēn.[Footnote 8] Tirunāmattukkāṇi - Kind of free-tenure denoting lands registered in the name of the deity.[Footnote 9] Tirunāmattāl.[Footnote 1] This is one of the three forms of the praśasti. The text is published in S. I. I., V, pp. 116-17,No. 302 (A. R. E. 14 of 1894). A. R. E. 338 of 1916 with the same praśasti is a grant givingastronomical details. The praśasti in this Inscription is full of mistakes and omissions and has beenrestored by comparison with No. 302 of S. I. I., V, pp. 116-17. The other forms of the praśastiof the King begin with "pū-tala-maṇandai" and "pū-tala-vaniṇai".[Footnote 2] The reading in the "Inscriptions (Texts) of the Pudukkkōṭṭai State". I, 20, is "pūvir ki-la-ti"which means the 3rd year. The 'Chronological List of Inscriptions of the Pudukkkōṭṭai State', p. 31,gives the year as '30'. This is a mistake as the year is too high for this King who is known tohave ruled for 27-28 years.[Footnote 3] The text reads 'pūvin-kilatti-mey-viriruppa' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'pūvin-kilatti-mēni-viriruppa'.[Footnote 4] The text reads 'mēdi-ni-(la)-mādu-nixi-yivapuna' where the (la) is superfluous and whatfollows is unintelligible. S. I. I., V, No. 302, has'makkalai-maṇandai-vākkiniḷ-viḷanga.'[Footnote 7] The text reads 'tikkiruṇandungum-viśai-nīl-verippa' while S. I. cells.location: On one of the walls of the Vishnu temple (now pulled down and reconstructed) at Mañjēri in the same taluk.
cells.remarks: Records an order of Kāngēya to the residents of Kāyānādu, remitting the taxes like kuṭṭanai, anttānyam, karparai-kkāryam-vēndu, from two of lands by Kudikkāl-kīl, which the villagers endowed for offerings to the two Pirāṭṭiyārs of Śilākōyivinnagaram- Embernān, for their welfare during the peril-in their village.

"Hail! Prosperity! In the third year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ Śrī
Sundara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar:
The ōlai(1) issued by Kāṅgaiyan(2), to be noted by the ūrār(3) of Muniyandai(4) :—
Whereas, in token of your gratitude for safe emergence from the peril
that visited your village,(5) you have endowed two mās of land, as measured
by the Kuḍitāṅgikkōl(6), in Muniandai-vayal as tiruvidaiyāttam(7) to
provide for the various requirements of the service and daily offerings of

(13) The text here is full of mistakes and reads 'pi-var-sembiyar-villava-āḍalar-pallamar-tirai-uṛuḍan-
murai-murai-pamiya' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has villavar-sembiyar-virādar-marātar-pallavar-tirai-
yuḍan-murai-murai-paniya.' Villavar - Cēras; Śembiyar - Cōlas; who the Viraṇḍar and Marātar were

(14) The text reads ' iru-nemin-āḷavam-oru-nedi-ōnga' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'iru-nēmi-yōḷavum
oru-nēmi-yōṅga'.
(15) The text reads ' innamuḍaiāḍipa-ilaviśai-nāṭam-manni-valara' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has
innamuḍu-ākiya-iyal-isai-nāṭam-manni-valara: Iyal - literary Tamil prose or poetry conforming
to the rules of grammar; isai - Tamil music; nāṭakam - Tamil literature pertaining to dances and
the drama.
(16) The text reads 'mani-aṇi-vira-simhāsantu-viḍarudaruḷiya-kōc-caḍaiyapanmarāna-trībhuvanac-
cakravartikai-śrī-Kulaśēkhara-Dēvar' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'mani-muḍi-sūḍi-kaḍiroḷi-vira
simhāsanativirvirundaruḷiya, etc. Vīrasimhasanam=throne of victory.
(16) Kadamai=government tax, probably paid in kind.
(17) Vari=tax paid in cash.
(18) Antarāyam=taxes levied by the local body.
(19) Tiruvodikālai or Tiruvodikāl was perhaps the old name of Malaívakkóvil.
(20) Chieftain of Kalvāyil nāḍu.
(1) Ṯlai=order from a king or person in authority. Literally it means the palm leaf on which the
order is written.
(2) Kāṅgaiyan or Gāṅgēyan—a local chieftain.
(3) Ūrār—the members of the village assembly or the residents of the village.
(4) Muniyandai—old name of Muniśandai.
(5) The text reads 'taṅgaḷ-ūril-vuḷuṅda-apāyattukku-nanmaikku-nanrāka (nanriyāka)?' The
nature of the peril referred to is not known. Probably it refers to a war.
(6) Kuḍitāṅgikkōl—a staff used as a unit of land measure.
(7) Tiruvidaiyāttam—a class of eleemosynary tenure denoting lands owned by a Viṣṇu temple.

We have hereby remitted therefrom, from this year onwards, all the dues

To this effect, this is the signature of Kāngaiyan. I, Uḍaiya-divākara-

text.inscription_text: 1 ஸ்வஸ்தி ஸ்ரீ [[*] திரிபுவனச்சக்கரவர்த்திகள் ஸ்ரீஸுந்தரவார[ண் டி]யதெ   வற்க்கு யாண்டு மூன்றாவது2 காக்கையன் ஒலை காணாட்டு முனிபந்தை ஊரார் கண்டு [[*] தங்களுரிள்   புருந்த அபாயதத்கு நன்[மை*]ய்க்கு3 நன்றாக திருமேற்கோவில் சொழக்கொன்விகண்கா எம்பெருமானுக்கு   எழுந்தருளி[க்*]த பிராட்டி-4 மார் இருவர்க்கு திருப்படியமாற்று உள்ளிட்ட நிமத்தங்களுக்கு முனிபக்-   தை வயலலி1 தாந்-5 கள் திருவிடையாட்டமாக குடிதாவிக்கொலால் விட்ட விலம் இரண்டு   மாவுக்கும் இறக்-6 க்ககடவ கடமை அந்தராயம் கற்ப்பூரவிலை காசியராட்சி மற்றும்   எப்பெபர்-7 ப்பட்[ட*] இதை குடிமைகளும் மற்றும் இவான்முதற் தந்தோம் [[*]   தாங்கள் விட்ட நிலத்திலெ8 இறையிலியாக மாட்டெறிந்து இப்படி சந்திராதித்தவற் செல்வதாக   கல்லிலும் செம்-9 பிலும் வெட்டிக்கொள்ள [[*] இப்படிக்கு காக்கையெனெழுத்து இப்ப-   டிக்கு உதய- 10 திவாகரமுவெந்த வெணர(ர)செ[ன்] [[*]
text.english_translation: "Hail! Prosperity! In the third year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ ŚrīSundara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar:The ōlai(1) issued by Kāṅgaiyan(2), to be noted by the ūrār(3) of Muniyandai(4) :—Whereas, in token of your gratitude for safe emergence from the perilthat visited your village,(5) you have endowed two mās of land, as measuredby the Kuḍitāṅgikkōl(6), in Muniandai-vayal as tiruvidaiyāttam(7) toprovide for the various requirements of the service and daily offerings of(13) The text here is full of mistakes and reads 'pi-var-sembiyar-villava-āḍalar-pallamar-tirai-uṛuḍan-murai-murai-pamiya' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has villavar-sembiyar-virādar-marātar-pallavar-tirai-yuḍan-murai-murai-paniya.' Villavar - Cēras; Śembiyar - Cōlas; who the Viraṇḍar and Marātar wereis not known.(14) The text reads ' iru-nemin-āḷavam-oru-nedi-ōnga' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'iru-nēmi-yōḷavumoru-nēmi-yōṅga'.(15) The text reads ' innamuḍaiāḍipa-ilaviśai-nāṭam-manni-valara' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 hasinnamuḍu-ākiya-iyal-isai-nāṭam-manni-valara: Iyal - literary Tamil prose or poetry conformingto the rules of grammar; isai - Tamil music; nāṭakam - Tamil literature pertaining to dances andthe drama.(16) The text reads 'mani-aṇi-vira-simhāsantu-viḍarudaruḷiya-kōc-caḍaiyapanmarāna-trībhuvanac-cakravartikai-śrī-Kulaśēkhara-Dēvar' while S. I. I., V, No. 302 has 'mani-muḍi-sūḍi-kaḍiroḷi-virasimhāsanativirvirundaruḷiya, etc. Vīrasimhasanam=throne of victory.(16) Kadamai=government tax, probably paid in kind.(17) Vari=tax paid in cash.(18) Antarāyam=taxes levied by the local body.(19) Tiruvodikālai or Tiruvodikāl was perhaps the old name of Malaívakkóvil.(20) Chieftain of Kalvāyil nāḍu.(1) Ṯlai=order from a king or person in authority. Literally it means the palm leaf on which theorder is written.(2) Kāṅgaiyan or Gāṅgēyan—a local chieftain.(3) Ūrār—the members of the village assembly or the residents of the village.(4) Muniyandai—old name of Muniśandai.(5) The text reads 'taṅgaḷ-ūril-vuḷuṅda-apāyattukku-nanmaikku-nanrāka (nanriyāka)?' Thenature of the peril referred to is not known. Probably it refers to a war.(6) Kuḍitāṅgikkōl—a staff used as a unit of land measure.(7) Tiruvidaiyāttam—a class of eleemosynary tenure denoting lands owned by a Viṣṇu temple.rice and other articles of food to the two Pirāṭṭimār of the Emberumānof Cōla-kón-viṇṇagaram in the Tirumérkóyil, who were installed andconsecrated:We have hereby remitted therefrom, from this year onwards, all the duessuch as kaḍamai, antarāyam, karpūravilai, kāriya-ārāyci and others.You shall therefore deem these lands, that you have thus endowed, asiraiyili, to continue so for so long as the moon and sun endure, and havethis inscribed so on stone.To this effect, this is the signature of Kāngaiyan. I, Uḍaiya-divākara-Múvéndavēlān, set my hand thus.

cells.location: On the south wall of the second prākāra in the Sikhāndīśvarasvāmin temple at Kuḍumiyāmalai in the Kulattūr taluk.
cells.date: 3rd year, Mangali. [Anu]pakshesha, Saturday, Maghaṁ, Pañchami. In A.D. 1218, on Saturday, 5th December, Dhanus bu. 5 and "Magha" commenced just before sunrise: they were both current throughout Saturday and came to end at '07 and 10 respectively on Sunday.
cells.remarks: A copy of an inscription of the 35th year of the reign of Tribhuvanachakra-vartin Śrī Kulōttuṅga-Chōlēśvara-dēva was reinscribed when the Dēvāna-maṇḍapa was renewed. Records an assignment of 25 kālam by the temple kshatriyas of Kuḍumīmalai, /1/dhaļiṅkōṇḍaśōla-vāḻnādu, for the daily offerings and other expenses in the temple of Tirumalai-kuḍumi-uḍaiya- Nāyanār.

cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! Whereas the course of stones on the northern side of the
sekadi and kumudam of the Tavanamandapam, on which an inscription
of former times was engraved, has to be covered and the stones re-arranged
in order to erect a tirumaṇḍapam for installing the Tirunaṭṭapperumāl,
a true copy of the inscription was taken:
































And whereas, in the third year of Sundara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar, in the month of
Maṅkaḷi, on Saturday, the fifth day(a) of the dark fortnight(1) when the
moon was in conjunction with the asterism of Makam, Ponnan Gāṅgēyan,
Lord of Arrūr, directed that the copy then taken(11), true to the original,
should be re-inscribed, the following is the copy thus re-inscribed :—
"Hail! Prosperity! In the 35th year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ Śrī
Kulōttuṅga Cōḷa Dēvar,(12) We, the Mūnrūpadai Porkōyil Kaikkōḷar(13) of
Iraṭṭapāḍikoṇḍacōḷavaḷanāḍu, also called Kōṇāḍu, made the following
provisions for the......
Kaikkōḷaṇāyakkara(14) and the Tambirāṭṭiyār(15), whom we installed and
consecrated in the temple of the Nāyanār of Tirunalakkunram(16) in Kuṇṟi-
yūrnāḍu of this nāḍu(17) :—
For the offerings of cooked rice(18) to this Dēvar, at the rate of four nāḷis(19) of
rice, as measured by the śulakkāl(20), for each sandhi(21), one kuruni(22) and
four nāḷis of rice for the three sandhis daily; and to the Tambirāttiyār, at
the rate of two nāḷis of rice for each sandhi, six nāḷis of rice daily;
amounting in all to one padakku(23) and two nāḷis of rice, corresponding
to five kuruṇis and five nāḷis of paddy at five measures of paddy to two of
rice(24);
For vegetables, pepper(25), ghee, betel-leaves and areca nuts(26) required for
offerings, one kuruni and one nāḷi of paddy;
For two offerings of śaṭṭicōru(27) during the mid-day sandhi one kuruni and
three nāḷis of paddy;
For the potter who makes the earthenware utensils two nāḷis of paddy for
each day;

(a) Pañcami.
(10) Aparāpakṣa.
(11) Aṉṟu-kal-veṭṭu-paḍi-yeḍutta-paḍiyē.
(12) Prof. K. A. N. Sastri, (Cōḷas II, ii, p. 709) identifies this King as Kulōttuṅga Cōḷa III,
(1178-1223 A. D.). Thus the date of the original grant would be 1212 A. D. This was only 6 years
before the re-inscription in 1218 A. D. (3rd year of Sundara Pāṇḍiya I, who came to the throne in
1216 A. D.) and must have been in the memory of the people. But in the beginning of the
inscription the grant is referred to as an inscription of former days (muṉṉāḷil) and thus the probability
seems to be the time of Kulōttuṅga Cōḷa I (1070-1122 A. D.)—it cannot be Kulōttuṅga II, who did
not rule for 35 years. Thus the date of the original grant seems to be 1104 A. D.
(13) The Mūnrūpadai-Porkōyil-Kaikkōḷar-figure in a grant of the 36th year of Kulōttuṅga I
in Kuḍumiyāmalai as the guardians of a trust. See P. S. I. 125 (A. R. E. 353 of 1904).
(14) Nandikēśvara—There are idols in stone and bronze of the standing forms of Nandikēśvara in
this temple.
(15) Tambirāṭṭiyār=the consort; the Dēvi of Nandikēśvara.
(16) Tirunalakkunram—old name for Kuḍumiyāmalai.
(17) Kōṇāḍu—province.
(18) Tiruvamudu śeydaruḷa.
(19) Nāḷi—grain measure also called paḍi.
(20) Śulakkāl—the standard grain measure used in Śiva temples, stamped with the trident (śūlam).
(21) Sandhi—time of worship or service: morning, noon and evening.
(22) Kuruṇi=8 nāḷis.
(23) Padakku=16 nāḷis.
(24) Añciravandāka.
(25) Kariyamudu & miḷakamudu.
(26) Adaikkāy-amudu.
(27) Śaṭṭicōru—rice cooked with sugar in earthen bowls and offered along with it.

And for the man who supplies fire-wood two nālis of paddy.
The supply of the above amount of paddy, amounting in all to 2 tūnis and 5
nālis, and the various expenses of the festival for three days in the months
of Mārkali, Māsi and Panguni when these deities are to be taken
out in procession, we undertake to meet from the 25 kāsu rendered with the
tiruppāvādai (28) in our villages which belong to this Dévar; and the
accountants (29) amongst us shall undertake the collection and payment every
year, for so long as the moon and sun endure.

In this manner, we, the Mūnrupadai Kaikkōlar made this endowment. May
the feet of those who protect this charity be on our heads. May those
who contemplate harm to this perish without progeny. May this be
protected by the nāttār (30). May this be protected by all Mahésvaras.

Footnotes:
[Footnote 8] Tiruppadimārru-uṭṭitta-nimandangajukku.
[Footnote 9] Pirāṭṭimār-divine consorts-Śrīdévi and Bhúdévi.
[Footnote 10] Emberumān-lit., my lord-here Viṣṇu.
[Footnote 11] Viṇṇagaram is a corruption of Viṣṇugraham, that is a Viṣṇu shrine. It was named after the
chieftain Cólakkón. The temple was called Tirumérkóyil-the holy western temple.
[Footnote 12] Kaḍamai-government tax; antarāyam-taxes levied by the local body; karpūravilai-
generally seems to mean price paid for temple lands; kāriya-ārāyci-cess paid for the superinten-
dence of transactions.
[Footnote 13] Iraiyili-tenures which are exempted from tax by the King.
[Footnote 14] Múvéndavēlān is one of the titles of the chiefs who were given administrative positions.
[Footnote 1] Yāṇḍu-múnrāvadu-Mārkaḷi-aparapaksam-Śanikkilamai-Makhamum-pañcamiyum-perraṇāḷ.
On Saturday 8th December 1218 A.D. Bahuḷā pañcami commenced at sunrise, and the lunar
conjunction with the asterism Makham just before sunrise and continued throughout Saturday,
and ended at 1.68 hrs. and 2.4 hrs. after sunrise respectively on Sunday.
[Footnote 2] Sékadi-Jagati or Jagadippadai-the course of stones of the top tier of the basement.
[Footnote 3] Kumudam-Kumudappadai or Kumudavari-the stones of the moulding in the plinth-the
course of stones with a semi-circular or hexagonal moulding.
[Footnote 4] Davanamandapam or Tavanamandapam-a maṇḍapam where the spring festival of a temple is
celebrated.
[Footnote 5] Kalvettana idam-tīrvitu-pār-paḍa-ittu.
[Footnote 6] Tirumaṇḍapam-Sacred maṇḍapam; here the Nṛttamaṇḍapam or the "hall of dance."
[Footnote 7] Tirunaṭṭapperumāl-the Lord who dances, viz., Natarāja.
[Footnote 8] Kalvett-up-padi-eduttu=-padi=true copy; here the copy taken on a palm-leaf.

text.remarks: A copy of an inscription of the 35th year of the reign of Tribhuvanachakra-vartin Śrī Kulōttuṅga-Chōlēśvara-dēva was reinscribed when the Dēvāna-maṇḍapa was renewed. Records an assignment of 25 kālam by the temple kshatriyas of Kuḍumīmalai, /1/dhaļiṅkōṇḍaśōla-vāḻnādu, for the daily offerings and other expenses in the temple of Tirumalai-kuḍumi-uḍaiya- Nāyanār.

Read வடலில்.2. Read திருநமண்டபம்.3. Read படி4.953 மி மா[தத்] . . . [ப]12 பக்ஷத்து ச(ன)னிக்கிழமை பெற்ற மகமும்பஞ்சமியும் பெற்ற அன்று கல்வெட்டு படியேடுத்தபடியே ஆற்றுரு-டையான் பொன்னன் காங்கேயன் வெ-4 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . றுசொல்ல வெட்டினபடியாவது [I*] ஹ்வஸ்ரீ [I*]திரிபுவனச்சக்கரவர்த்திகள் ஸ்ரீ குலோத்துங்கசோழதெவற்கு யாண்டுஙுங் வது கொளுடான இரட்டபாடிகொண்-5 டசோழவளநாட்டு மூன்றுபடை பொற்கொயில் கைக்கொண்டுரொம்இன்னுஞு குன்றிருஞாட்டு திருகைக்குன்றம் உடைய நாயனார் கோவிலில்காங்கள் எழுந்தருளினி-6 . . . . . . . . . . . . . வக்கொலநாய்கரும தம்பிராட்டியார்[க*]கும் திருவமுது எழுந்தருள இத்தெவர் கோவிலில் குலாகலால் நாள் ஒன்றுக்குசந்தி ஒன்றுக்கு திருஅமுது அரிசி காணுதியா-7 க சந்தி மு[றுக்கு] அரிசி துளி¹ காணுதியும் [*] தம்பிராட்டியாற்குசந்தி ஒன்று அரிசி இருநாழியாக அரிசி அறுகாழியும் [*] ஆக நாள்ஒன்றுக்கு அரிசி பதக்கு² இருநாழியும் ஆஞ் . . . 8 ரண்டாரீ கொன்று ஐங்குறுணி ஐஞ்சுநாழியும் [*] கறியமதுுக்கும் மிள[க]-மோதுக்கும் செய்யமுதுக்கும் அடைக்காயமுதக்கும் நெல்லு குறுணிஒருநாழியும் [I*] மத்தி[ரன[ச்ச்]சிகிக்கு சட்-9 டிசொறு இரண்டுக்கு நெல்லு குறுணி முன்னாழியும் [*] கலமிங்குசவ-னுக்கு கா[க]சுக்கு நெல்லு இருநாழியுஞ் [*] விறகிவோனுக்கு நெல்லுஇருநாழியும் [I*] ஆத் நாள் க க்கு . . . 10 நல்லது உதகு³க்கும மார்கழியும் (யாழகழியும்) மாசியும் பங்குனியும் திரு-விழா எழுச்³சருளு நாள மூன்றுக்கு வெண்டும் பல அழிவுக்கு இத்-தெவர் ஊர்களில் திரு-11 ப்பாடைக்கு வை(னை)ய்க்குங்காச ம்மிடும் எற்களில்*] க[ண்]க்குவார்² ஆண்டுதொறும் எரெட்டிக்கொண்டு சந்திராதித்தவழ்செலுத்தக்கடவோமாகவும் [I*] இப்படி குடுத்தோம் மு-12 ன்றுபடையைக்கைக்கொளரொம் [I*] இத்தன்மை நிலைநிறுத்துவர் சிபா-தங்கள் எங்கள் தலைமெலன [I*] இ[ச்]சுகுத்துஇ கிளைப்பர் வழியு-றுவார் [I*] இது நாட்டார் க[ஷை] [I*] இது பன்மதெஹ-13 னரி கீௗை உ . . .
text.english_translation: "Hail! Prosperity! Whereas the course of stones on the northern side of thesekadi and kumudam of the Tavanamandapam, on which an inscriptionof former times was engraved, has to be covered and the stones re-arrangedin order to erect a tirumaṇḍapam for installing the Tirunaṭṭapperumāl,a true copy of the inscription was taken:And whereas, in the third year of Sundara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar, in the month ofMaṅkaḷi, on Saturday, the fifth day(a) of the dark fortnight(1) when themoon was in conjunction with the asterism of Makam, Ponnan Gāṅgēyan,Lord of Arrūr, directed that the copy then taken(11), true to the original,should be re-inscribed, the following is the copy thus re-inscribed :—"Hail! Prosperity! In the 35th year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ ŚrīKulōttuṅga Cōḷa Dēvar,(12) We, the Mūnrūpadai Porkōyil Kaikkōḷar(13) ofIraṭṭapāḍikoṇḍacōḷavaḷanāḍu, also called Kōṇāḍu, made the followingprovisions for the......Kaikkōḷaṇāyakkara(14) and the Tambirāṭṭiyār(15), whom we installed andconsecrated in the temple of the Nāyanār of Tirunalakkunram(16) in Kuṇṟi-yūrnāḍu of this nāḍu(17) :—For the offerings of cooked rice(18) to this Dēvar, at the rate of four nāḷis(19) ofrice, as measured by the śulakkāl(20), for each sandhi(21), one kuruni(22) andfour nāḷis of rice for the three sandhis daily; and to the Tambirāttiyār, atthe rate of two nāḷis of rice for each sandhi, six nāḷis of rice daily;amounting in all to one padakku(23) and two nāḷis of rice, correspondingto five kuruṇis and five nāḷis of paddy at five measures of paddy to two ofrice(24);For vegetables, pepper(25), ghee, betel-leaves and areca nuts(26) required forofferings, one kuruni and one nāḷi of paddy;For two offerings of śaṭṭicōru(27) during the mid-day sandhi one kuruni andthree nāḷis of paddy;For the potter who makes the earthenware utensils two nāḷis of paddy foreach day;(a) Pañcami.(10) Aparāpakṣa.(11) Aṉṟu-kal-veṭṭu-paḍi-yeḍutta-paḍiyē.(12) Prof. K. A. N. Sastri, (Cōḷas II, ii, p. 709) identifies this King as Kulōttuṅga Cōḷa III,(1178-1223 A. D.). Thus the date of the original grant would be 1212 A. D. This was only 6 yearsbefore the re-inscription in 1218 A. D. (3rd year of Sundara Pāṇḍiya I, who came to the throne in1216 A. D.) and must have been in the memory of the people. But in the beginning of theinscription the grant is referred to as an inscription of former days (muṉṉāḷil) and thus the probabilityseems to be the time of Kulōttuṅga Cōḷa I (1070-1122 A. D.)—it cannot be Kulōttuṅga II, who didnot rule for 35 years. Thus the date of the original grant seems to be 1104 A. D.(13) The Mūnrūpadai-Porkōyil-Kaikkōḷar-figure in a grant of the 36th year of Kulōttuṅga Iin Kuḍumiyāmalai as the guardians of a trust. See P. S. I. 125 (A. R. E. 353 of 1904).(14) Nandikēśvara—There are idols in stone and bronze of the standing forms of Nandikēśvara inthis temple.(15) Tambirāṭṭiyār=the consort; the Dēvi of Nandikēśvara.(16) Tirunalakkunram—old name for Kuḍumiyāmalai.(17) Kōṇāḍu—province.(18) Tiruvamudu śeydaruḷa.(19) Nāḷi—grain measure also called paḍi.(20) Śulakkāl—the standard grain measure used in Śiva temples, stamped with the trident (śūlam).(21) Sandhi—time of worship or service: morning, noon and evening.(22) Kuruṇi=8 nāḷis.(23) Padakku=16 nāḷis.(24) Añciravandāka.(25) Kariyamudu & miḷakamudu.(26) Adaikkāy-amudu.(27) Śaṭṭicōru—rice cooked with sugar in earthen bowls and offered along with it.And for the man who supplies fire-wood two nālis of paddy.The supply of the above amount of paddy, amounting in all to 2 tūnis and 5nālis, and the various expenses of the festival for three days in the monthsof Mārkali, Māsi and Panguni when these deities are to be takenout in procession, we undertake to meet from the 25 kāsu rendered with thetiruppāvādai (28) in our villages which belong to this Dévar; and theaccountants (29) amongst us shall undertake the collection and payment everyyear, for so long as the moon and sun endure.In this manner, we, the Mūnrupadai Kaikkōlar made this endowment. Maythe feet of those who protect this charity be on our heads. May thosewho contemplate harm to this perish without progeny. May this beprotected by the nāttār (30). May this be protected by all Mahésvaras.Footnotes:[Footnote 8] Tiruppadimārru-uṭṭitta-nimandangajukku.[Footnote 9] Pirāṭṭimār-divine consorts-Śrīdévi and Bhúdévi.[Footnote 10] Emberumān-lit., my lord-here Viṣṇu.[Footnote 11] Viṇṇagaram is a corruption of Viṣṇugraham, that is a Viṣṇu shrine. It was named after thechieftain Cólakkón. The temple was called Tirumérkóyil-the holy western temple.[Footnote 12] Kaḍamai-government tax; antarāyam-taxes levied by the local body; karpūravilai-generally seems to mean price paid for temple lands; kāriya-ārāyci-cess paid for the superinten-dence of transactions.[Footnote 13] Iraiyili-tenures which are exempted from tax by the King.[Footnote 14] Múvéndavēlān is one of the titles of the chiefs who were given administrative positions.[Footnote 1] Yāṇḍu-múnrāvadu-Mārkaḷi-aparapaksam-Śanikkilamai-Makhamum-pañcamiyum-perraṇāḷ.On Saturday 8th December 1218 A.D. Bahuḷā pañcami commenced at sunrise, and the lunarconjunction with the asterism Makham just before sunrise and continued throughout Saturday,and ended at 1.68 hrs. and 2.4 hrs. after sunrise respectively on Sunday.[Footnote 2] Sékadi-Jagati or Jagadippadai-the course of stones of the top tier of the basement.[Footnote 3] Kumudam-Kumudappadai or Kumudavari-the stones of the moulding in the plinth-thecourse of stones with a semi-circular or hexagonal moulding.[Footnote 4] Davanamandapam or Tavanamandapam-a maṇḍapam where the spring festival of a temple iscelebrated.[Footnote 5] Kalvettana idam-tīrvitu-pār-paḍa-ittu.[Footnote 6] Tirumaṇḍapam-Sacred maṇḍapam; here the Nṛttamaṇḍapam or the "hall of dance."[Footnote 7] Tirunaṭṭapperumāl-the Lord who dances, viz., Natarāja.[Footnote 8] Kalvett-up-padi-eduttu=-padi=true copy; here the copy taken on a palm-leaf.

cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land in public auction selling once, twice, thrice, by certain persons of Siḍḍamallūr in Kumaṅgīl-nādu, a sub-division of Tenkaṅgai-nādu, to one Nambi Pillai-mālakkilakkan alias Cēyīrāju Rāyar of Āvūr in Sīda-Pāndya-vāḻnādu for 25 palasurukku-poṇ (then genuine old coin).

கொணட்டுக்குன்றூஞாட்டுச்சிகாலலூர் திருவானான் சொழமுவெக்-

2. பார் கொடண்டலும் கந்தகொழுந்தும் கந்தன்கணியும் ம்பிகொழுந்தும்
நம்பிபத்மலும் பொன்னன் ஒன்றாயிரமுடையானும் இவ்வனைவோரம்
நீங்கள் கிழைபுன்செய் விலைக்[கு]ற விக்கக்கொள்விகொளிரோவென்று]
ஒருகலாவதுமிருகாலவ-

ருடையான் நம்பி பொன்னம்பலக்கூத்தானை உடையவர் நங்ஜெயொராயர்
கொள்வெ[ன்று] அருளிச்செய்ய முன்சொல்லப்பட்ட இவ்வனை-
வசெரம் நாங்கள் விற்கிற பு-

4 ன்செய்க்குப்பெருநான்கெல்லையாவன [*] கீழ்பாற்கெல்லே மெய்மண-

வாளர்சொலெமுவத்தெவ[ள]ன் [செய்க்கு] வடக்கும் [*] மெல்பார்-
செல்லை கந்தன்கொழுந்தும் நம்பிகொழு-

cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the 3rd year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikal Sundara
Pāndiya Dévar, who was pleased to take Sōnādu, (1) also called Kó-Māra-
varman:

Whereas, we Tiruvālan Cóla Mūvéndavēlān, Tiruvudaiyān Kōdandan, Sundan
Kōlundu, Sundan Kani, Nambi Kōlundu, Nambi Panman and Ponnan
Onrāyiramudaiyan, all of us, jointly, offering to sell our land called Kilai-
puncey to any one who would bid for it, called out so once, twice,
and thrice (2), and Udaiyār Gāngéyarāyār, also called Nambi Ponnambalak-
kūttan, chief of Arrūr, (3) was pleased to reply that he would take it;

We, the aforesaid vendors, having declared the following four boundaries of
the land that we offered for sale-eastern boundary to the west of the
common boundary of the village of Mélmananallūr; southern boundary to
the north of the sey (4) belonging to Tiruvalar sōlai Mūvéndavēlān; western
boundary to the east of the four boundaries of the sey belonging to Sundan
Kōlundu, Nambi Kōlundu, and Tiruvan Cóla Mūvéndavēlān, and northern
boundary to the south of the dry lands belonging to Ponnan Onrāyira-
mudaiyān, Sundan Kōlundu, and Nambi Kōlundu-made over the dry

(28) Tiruppāvādai-offering of a heap of cooked rice on a new cloth spread on the ground. This
forms the offering made by a whole community.

(29) Kanakku-eluduvār.

(30) Nāttār-the representatives of the nādu.

text.inscription_text: 1 ஹ்வஸ்ரீ [I*] கொமாரபர்மனான திரிபுவனச்ச்க[ர*]வத்திகள் சொளுடுகொண்டு அருளிய சுந்தரபாண்டியதெவற்கு யாண்டு ஙு ஆவது தென்கொணட்டுக்குன்றூஞாட்டுச்சிகாலலூர் திருவானான் சொழமுவெக்-தவெளானும் திருவுடை-1. cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the third year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ Śrī
Sundara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar, who was pleased to take Śōṉāḍu, also called Śrī
Kō-Māravarman, who, while the Goddess of fortune, seated on the lotus
flower², and the Goddess of the Earth³ abode on his shoulders, the Goddess
of learning, who resides in the tongue⁴, and the Goddess of Victory⁵ were
abundantly benign, the ensigns of the mighty and ferocious Tiger⁶ and the
cruel Bow⁷ were struck and went into hiding⁸, and the ensign of the
brilliant (double) carp⁹ was sporting on the top of the famous golden











































elephants that trumpeted the roaring sea and high bred horses(24), was seated enthroned, along with Uḷakamuḷuḍuḍaiyāḷ, his queen, on the famous Vīra siṃgātanam wrought with jewels, so that the code laid down by Manu, who was created by the God seated on the dewy white lotus with heads facing all the four directions(25), may well prevail:—

The text of the royal order graciously issued(26):—

Whereas, Piḷḷaiyār Aḻagapperumāḷ made an appeal to the Nāyanār(28), requesting that the burden of irai(29) that was being levied from the villages of Añjanamaṅgalam, also called Aṉumaṉtāi, and Tiruṉavālūr in Tuṟumā-nāḍu in Virudharājabhayaṅkaravalaṉāḍu, also called Kāṉanāḍu, should be lightened as an act of dedication for the bodily welfare of Uḷakuḍaiya-nāyaṉār(30), and on reminding the king about it, was pleased to obtain gracious assent, the following are the terms of the royal order, thus obtained with oblations of water(31):—

For lands on which crops are full grown and accepted as first class(32) shall be paid five kalams, two tūnis one paḍakku and four nāḻis(33) of paddy for every mā of land after a reduction of two kalams for every mā of land(34).

For those lands which are classified as nirili-nilam(35) in these villages, paying taxes in accordance with the varisai(36) prevailing therein, shall be paid three kalams, two tūṇis, three kuṟuṇis and three uḷakkus of paddy for every mā of land.

For lands under navirai crop(38) shall be paid an amount of paddy in the ratio of three quarters to one of the above rate.

For lands under varagu(39) shall be paid an amount of paddy in the ratio of a half to one of the same rate.

(24) Kaḍalēṉa-muḷaṅgum kari-nalliyāṉai-vaḍapula-vēṉḍar-maṇi-puyam-piriyā-ilaṅgilai-yarivaiyar-toḷudu-niṉṟēṉa.
Kari=elephant; Nalliyāṉ = high bred horses; Nalliyāṉai can also mean 'cow-elephant' while kari means 'bull-elephant.'
(25) Paṇi-malar-tāmarai-tiśai-mukan-paḍaitta-maṉu-neri-taḷaippa-maṇi-muḍi-śūḍi.
(26) Prasādam-śeydu-aruḷiṉa-tirumukappaḍi; tiru-mukam=royal order, lit. oral orders issued by the king.
(28) Piḷḷaiyār Aḻagapperumāḷ—The title Piḷḷaiyār was given to relatives of the King and other officers in close attendance, as a mark of endearment. Aḻagapperumāḷ, according to A. R. E. 183 of 1935-36, 216 of 1914, and 77 of 1916, was the brother-in-law of the Emperor.
(29) Nāyanār—Respectful reference to the Emperor.
(30) Irai—Government taxes.
(31) Uḷakuḍaiya-nāyaṉār—The form in which the Emperor is always referred to.
(32) Nāyanārkku-viṉṇappam-śeydu-niṉaippumiṭṭu-niṟum-vārttu-taruvittu-aruḷiṉa-prasādam-śeydaruḷiṉa-tirumukappaḍi.
(33) Payreḷuda-mudal-koṇḍa-nilattukku.
(34) 5 kalams = 96 x 5 measures; 2 tuṇi = 32 x 2 measures; 1 paḍakku = 16 measures; 4 nāḻi = 4 measures.
(35) The reduction from the previous rate, viz 2 kalams = 96 x 2 measures.
(36) Nirili-nilam—lit., water-less lands. Perhaps this refers to lands where there is scarcity of water. They could not have been dry lands, since paddy is said to be grown on them.
(37) Varisai—rates of assessment.
(38) 3 kalams = 96 x 3 measures; 2 tūṇis = 32 x 2 measures; 3 kuṟuṇis = 8 x 3 measures; 3 uḷakkus = 1 x 3 measures.
(39) Navirai—a variety of paddy sown usually in the month of Āḍi—July-August.
(40) Varagu—Common millet—Paspalum scorbiculatum.

For lands under gingelly and tinai(40) shall be paid an amount of paddy in the
ratio of a quarter to one of the same rate.
Whenever Ulakuḍaiyaṇāyaṉār(41) is pleased to visit all taxes, primarily
tiruveḷuccikkaḍamai(42) and others of diverse kind, levied by the nāḍu shall
be paid in the ratio of a half to one and the supply of veṭṭi and muṭṭai-āḷ(43)
shall not be obligatory.
In accordance with the order issued by royal pleasure, I, Avaṉinārāyaṇa
Dévaṉ(44), inscribed this on stone, stipulating the payment of these taxes
for the villages of Tirunāvalūr, a brahmadēyam village and Añjaṉamaṅgalam,
also called Arumaṉāḷi. May this prosper.

Footnotes:
[Footnote 5] Aruṇādu-nar paḷankāsu - current genuine old kāśu; this indicates that coins issued by previous
rulers of the territory were current, provided they were genuine and in good condition.
[Footnote 6] Āvaṇakkalaṁ - the place where sale transactions were registered, something like a registration
office.
[Footnote 7] Katti-ērri.
[Footnote 8] Koṇ-cilavarakkoṇḍu.
[Footnote 9] Vilaipramāṇam.
[Footnote 1] This is the only form of praśasti found in the inscriptions in the State - P. S. I. 250, 256,
290, and 323. The other form beginning with 'pū-maruviya tirumādum' etc., is not found in the
inscriptions in the State.
[Footnote 2] Pū-maruviya-tirumadaṇtaiyum.
[Footnote 3] The text reads 'Jayamadantaiyum' which is a mistake. P. S. I. 256, 290, and 323, and others
from outside the State read 'Puvi-madantai' which is correct. The Emperor is likened to
Viṣṇu, whose manifestation on earth he was believed to be by the Hindus, and the two consorts of
Viṣṇu viz., Śrī Dēvi or Tirumadaṇtai, and Bhū Dēvi, or Puvimadaṇtai, should be associated with
the Emperor, signifying fortune and territory.
[Footnote 4] Nā-maruviya-kalai-madantai.
[Footnote 5] Jayamadantai.
[Footnote 6] Kōlāṇṭa-siṇap-puliyum. This refers to the tiger ensign of the Cōḷas.
[Footnote 7] Koḍum-silaiyum. This refers to the bow ensign of the Cēras.
[Footnote 8] Kulaindu-olippa.
[Footnote 9] Varikkayal-kal. This refers to the ensign of the Pāṇḍiyas with the emblem of the double carp
(Kayal) - Cyprinus fimbriatus.

text.inscription_text: 1 லஸூ ஸ்ரீ [*] பூமருவிய திருமடந்தைபுஞ்செயமடந்தையும் புயத்திருப்பநாமருவிய2 கலைமடந்தையுஞ்செயமடந்தையு[ம்] கல[ஞ்சி]ரப்பக்கொளாத சினப்புரி-யுல்-3 கொடுஞ்சிநிலையுங்கலைந்தொளிப்ப வாளார்ந்த பொற்சிசிமெல் [வரி]க்கேபல்கள்கொல் நடப்ப ஒரு கு-4 வினைபாட இருங்க[ட]ல் வலைப்பத்திரம்பெரு[க்க்குக]லி கடித்து செல்-கொல் நடப்ப ஒரு கு-5 டை கிழவநிருலவிகுன்னீர முலகைத்தமிழுமுமுறைமை[யி]ல் விளங்க நால்வகைவெதமு [ம்*] [கனின்றுடன்]6 லா ஐவகை [வெ]ழ்வியுஞ்செய்கினியெற்ற அறவணச்செசமையமுமுழு-குடந்திகழ எழு1. Read perhaps கந்தகொழுந்து கம்பிகொழுந்து திருவன் சோழமுழுவெந்தவேளான் இவர்கள்2. Read பொன்னன்.3. Read கந்தகொழுந்து நம்பிகொழுந்து இவர்கள்.4. Read இரண்டையும்.5. Read ஆவணக்கெ[த்]தே[கா]ட்டேற்றி.6. Read காங் கியை.7. Read கொடண்டலும்.8. Read கந்தன் கொழுத்தனும்.9. Read கந்தன் கணியும்.10. Read பன்மனும்.21. Read இவ்வனைவோரும்.[photographic plate, script not transcribed]
text.english_translation: "Hail! Prosperity! In the third year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikaḷ ŚrīSundara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar, who was pleased to take Śōṉāḍu, also called ŚrīKō-Māravarman, who, while the Goddess of fortune, seated on the lotusflower², and the Goddess of the Earth³ abode on his shoulders, the Goddessof learning, who resides in the tongue⁴, and the Goddess of Victory⁵ wereabundantly benign, the ensigns of the mighty and ferocious Tiger⁶ and thecruel Bow⁷ were struck and went into hiding⁸, and the ensign of thebrilliant (double) carp⁹ was sporting on the top of the famous goldenelephants that trumpeted the roaring sea and high bred horses(24), was seated enthroned, along with Uḷakamuḷuḍuḍaiyāḷ, his queen, on the famous Vīra siṃgātanam wrought with jewels, so that the code laid down by Manu, who was created by the God seated on the dewy white lotus with heads facing all the four directions(25), may well prevail:—The text of the royal order graciously issued(26):—Whereas, Piḷḷaiyār Aḻagapperumāḷ made an appeal to the Nāyanār(28), requesting that the burden of irai(29) that was being levied from the villages of Añjanamaṅgalam, also called Aṉumaṉtāi, and Tiruṉavālūr in Tuṟumā-nāḍu in Virudharājabhayaṅkaravalaṉāḍu, also called Kāṉanāḍu, should be lightened as an act of dedication for the bodily welfare of Uḷakuḍaiya-nāyaṉār(30), and on reminding the king about it, was pleased to obtain gracious assent, the following are the terms of the royal order, thus obtained with oblations of water(31):—For lands on which crops are full grown and accepted as first class(32) shall be paid five kalams, two tūnis one paḍakku and four nāḻis(33) of paddy for every mā of land after a reduction of two kalams for every mā of land(34).For those lands which are classified as nirili-nilam(35) in these villages, paying taxes in accordance with the varisai(36) prevailing therein, shall be paid three kalams, two tūṇis, three kuṟuṇis and three uḷakkus of paddy for every mā of land.For lands under navirai crop(38) shall be paid an amount of paddy in the ratio of three quarters to one of the above rate.For lands under varagu(39) shall be paid an amount of paddy in the ratio of a half to one of the same rate.(24) Kaḍalēṉa-muḷaṅgum kari-nalliyāṉai-vaḍapula-vēṉḍar-maṇi-puyam-piriyā-ilaṅgilai-yarivaiyar-toḷudu-niṉṟēṉa.Kari=elephant; Nalliyāṉ = high bred horses; Nalliyāṉai can also mean 'cow-elephant' while kari means 'bull-elephant.'(25) Paṇi-malar-tāmarai-tiśai-mukan-paḍaitta-maṉu-neri-taḷaippa-maṇi-muḍi-śūḍi.(26) Prasādam-śeydu-aruḷiṉa-tirumukappaḍi; tiru-mukam=royal order, lit. oral orders issued by the king.(28) Piḷḷaiyār Aḻagapperumāḷ—The title Piḷḷaiyār was given to relatives of the King and other officers in close attendance, as a mark of endearment. Aḻagapperumāḷ, according to A. R. E. 183 of 1935-36, 216 of 1914, and 77 of 1916, was the brother-in-law of the Emperor.(29) Nāyanār—Respectful reference to the Emperor.(30) Irai—Government taxes.(31) Uḷakuḍaiya-nāyaṉār—The form in which the Emperor is always referred to.(32) Nāyanārkku-viṉṇappam-śeydu-niṉaippumiṭṭu-niṟum-vārttu-taruvittu-aruḷiṉa-prasādam-śeydaruḷiṉa-tirumukappaḍi.(33) Payreḷuda-mudal-koṇḍa-nilattukku.(34) 5 kalams = 96 x 5 measures; 2 tuṇi = 32 x 2 measures; 1 paḍakku = 16 measures; 4 nāḻi = 4 measures.(35) The reduction from the previous rate, viz 2 kalams = 96 x 2 measures.(36) Nirili-nilam—lit., water-less lands. Perhaps this refers to lands where there is scarcity of water. They could not have been dry lands, since paddy is said to be grown on them.(37) Varisai—rates of assessment.(38) 3 kalams = 96 x 3 measures; 2 tūṇis = 32 x 2 measures; 3 kuṟuṇis = 8 x 3 measures; 3 uḷakkus = 1 x 3 measures.(39) Navirai—a variety of paddy sown usually in the month of Āḍi—July-August.(40) Varagu—Common millet—Paspalum scorbiculatum.For lands under gingelly and tinai(40) shall be paid an amount of paddy in theratio of a quarter to one of the same rate.Whenever Ulakuḍaiyaṇāyaṉār(41) is pleased to visit all taxes, primarilytiruveḷuccikkaḍamai(42) and others of diverse kind, levied by the nāḍu shallbe paid in the ratio of a half to one and the supply of veṭṭi and muṭṭai-āḷ(43)shall not be obligatory.In accordance with the order issued by royal pleasure, I, AvaṉinārāyaṇaDévaṉ(44), inscribed this on stone, stipulating the payment of these taxesfor the villages of Tirunāvalūr, a brahmadēyam village and Añjaṉamaṅgalam,also called Arumaṉāḷi. May this prosper.Footnotes:[Footnote 5] Aruṇādu-nar paḷankāsu - current genuine old kāśu; this indicates that coins issued by previousrulers of the territory were current, provided they were genuine and in good condition.[Footnote 6] Āvaṇakkalaṁ - the place where sale transactions were registered, something like a registrationoffice.[Footnote 7] Katti-ērri.[Footnote 8] Koṇ-cilavarakkoṇḍu.[Footnote 9] Vilaipramāṇam.[Footnote 1] This is the only form of praśasti found in the inscriptions in the State - P. S. I. 250, 256,290, and 323. The other form beginning with 'pū-maruviya tirumādum' etc., is not found in theinscriptions in the State.[Footnote 2] Pū-maruviya-tirumadaṇtaiyum.[Footnote 3] The text reads 'Jayamadantaiyum' which is a mistake. P. S. I. 256, 290, and 323, and othersfrom outside the State read 'Puvi-madantai' which is correct. The Emperor is likened toViṣṇu, whose manifestation on earth he was believed to be by the Hindus, and the two consorts ofViṣṇu viz., Śrī Dēvi or Tirumadaṇtai, and Bhū Dēvi, or Puvimadaṇtai, should be associated withthe Emperor, signifying fortune and territory.[Footnote 4] Nā-maruviya-kalai-madantai.[Footnote 5] Jayamadantai.[Footnote 6] Kōlāṇṭa-siṇap-puliyum. This refers to the tiger ensign of the Cōḷas.[Footnote 7] Koḍum-silaiyum. This refers to the bow ensign of the Cēras.[Footnote 8] Kulaindu-olippa.[Footnote 9] Varikkayal-kal. This refers to the ensign of the Pāṇḍiyas with the emblem of the double carp(Kayal) - Cyprinus fimbriatus.

cells.location: Same taluk, Neipasal, in the Ahastisvarar temple, in the front mandapa, a record

cells.tamil_fields: header_tamil: மேற்படி தாலுகா, நெய்பாசால், அஹஸ்தீவர்கோவிலில் முன்மண்டபதியுள்ள சாசனம்,-
cells.inscription_text:
1. ஸ்வஸ்தி ஸ்ரீ [*] கோமாறமன்மாரானை திரிபுவனச்சக்கரவர்த்திகள் ஸ்ரீசுந்தர-

கிழமை-
2. யும் பெற்ற மூலத்து நாள் கண்டனுதைபஞ்சேட்ஸாடனான காங்கய-

3. சி வயக்கலும் [ஆல]ந்திடயிலும் இதிற்நீணெற்று கரும்டூருணி தென்-
மூலைக்கிறைம திடயுமா சிராதத்துகூட வயலில் மணியிலக்கலு-
4. ம் மக்கது இறத்தவரும் அச்ச்கலவி பொன்வரி நாடேன்றவரி மற்று-
ம்பெறப்பட்டகருந்தவந்து இங்காயனாற்கு இறையிலி காராண்கிமை-
யாகத்தங்கு-
5. [தாம்][[*]][இப்படிக்குச்சந்திராதி]த்தவரை செல்வதாக கல்வெட்டிக்-
குடுத்தேன் கண்டன் உரையஞ்செய்தாரானை
6. [காங்கெனன்] ... ... மூவானாக இல்லை . . . .
பன்னெஹெமைா [ச*]தெெஉ [[*]]

"Hail! Prosperity! In the 4th year of Tribhuvaṉaccakravartikaḷ Śrī
Suṉdara Pāṇḍiya Dévar, also called Kó-Māravarmaṉ, in the month of
Riṣabha on the third day of the (dark) fortnight, a Saturday when the
moon was in conjunction with the asterism of Mūlam, as an endowment to the
Nāyaṉār of Nelvāyil(45), I, Gāṅgēyarayaṉ, also called Kaṉḍaṉ Uḍaiyaṉjeydaṉ,
gave the following, among the lands of this place, viz. Ilāśivayakkaḷ(46) lands,
Alaṉtuḍaval lands(47), the Karuṉṭūruṉṉi(48) with the well therein, the well at
the southern corner, and the tiḍal(49), and in Śirāttākkuḍi hamlet, the
Maṉivayakkaḷ lands, after exempting therefrom the accuvāri, poṉvāri(50),

(40) Tiṉai—millet—Setaria italica.
(41) Ulakuḍaiya-Nāyaṉār—the Lord of the Earth viz., the Emperor.
(42) Tiruveḷuccik-kaḍamai—tax levied during royal visits or marches. It is interesting to note
that a similar cess called savāri kāryam was levied in the State till the beginning of this century to
furnish supplies to the Raja and the principal officers on tour. See Revised State Manual p. 377.
(43) Veṭṭi-muṭṭai-āḷ or veṭṭi-muṭṭā-vāḷ—supply of free labour, to be employed for public purposes, or
free food given to those so employed.
(44) The local officer who enforced the order.
* Iṣaba (Riṣabha or Vaikāśi), tutikai (titiyai), Saṉikkilamai, Mūlam. Whether the fortnight
was the dark or the bright fortnight is not mentioned. On Saturday, May 4th, 1219 A. D. the
third tithi (tṛtīyai) and not the second (tvitīyai) ended at 42 of the day after sunrise, and the lunar
conjunction with the Nakṣatra, Mūlam, ended at 33 of the day after sunrise. The fortnight must have
been the dark fortnight or bahuḷa-pakṣa. Probably tutikai is a mistake for tritikai.
(45) Nelvāyil—the old name of Neivāsal.
(46) Ilāśivayakkaḷ—the name of a plot of improved wet-land (vayakkaḷ).
(47) Alaṉtuḍaval—garden land or plantation (tuḍaval) named so probably because of its association
with the banyan tree (Ālam).
(48) Karuṉṭūruṉṉi—probably Kuruntu-ūruṉṉi—the public drinking-water tank or well (ūr-uṉṉi).
Ūruṉṉi is now corrupted into uruṉi or ūraṉi.
(49) Tiḍal—open space or uncultivated land.
(50) Accuvāri—taxes paid in cash; poṉ-vāri—taxes paid in gold.

cells.inscription_text:
1 ஸ்வஸ்தி ஸ்ரீ [*] திரிபுவனச்சுரவத்திகள்
2 சொணமுகொண்டருளிய சுக்கிரபாண்டி [ய]
3 தெவற்கு யாண்டு ச வது கெளசிக்தவ-
4 னாட்டு கல்லவாயிரட்டு நெலவாவி-
5 ல் திருவ[த்]திரை [மு*]கடைய காமாற்கு வர்-
6 ற்பூக நாழிற்று யெ திபதி பெற்ற புதன்
7 கிழமை நாள் கண்டன் ஆ[வு]டை-
8 யாராக கல்லவாயிரழாழ்வர்கொ[]
9 இவற் திரு[த்]த[ல]வித்தியாமுகடைய காவநாற்[ற்] செ-
10 பகயீ காச்சிபற்கு பெருமாள் தெவர் நிலமா-
11 க சிங்கங்குராதி வயக்கல் வரையில் இரண்டு-
12 ம் குவளசெய்யும் அழகுண்ட பல்லவந-
13 தரையன் பல்வெ ள[நான்*] விசெயொண்ட தொட்-
14 டமும் உள்பட நிலம் இறைப்படி சிலம் ஓ-
15 ருமாலைக்கும் இப்பெரியகாச்சியார்-
16 கு ஒரு மாச்செய்[ய்]க்கு எப்பெறப்பட்ட இ-
17 றையும் உள்பட இருகல லரையா
18 றை விளுப்பாடாக சீர்வாத்துர்க்கு-
19 கித்தென் கண்டாவுடைவரகாதா
20 கல்லவாயினடாழவரென [[*]] பெரிவளச்சி
21 இக்கடிபெருமான்தெவசெய் இறப்பானு-
22 கீ[I][*] இது பக்மாஹெவரா [க]க்ஷ[]

1. Read பன்மரசன.
2. Read காடராயர்கோல்.
3. Read பெரிய.
4. Read பலவத்தரையக.
5. Read வரையாத.
6. Read இறை.
7. Read சீர் வார்த்தை.
8. Read probably பெரியகாச்சியாற்கு இப்படி பெருமாள்தெவர்கெ இறுப்பானாக.

cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the 4th year of Tribhuvaṉaccakravartikaḷ Śrī
Suṅdara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar, who was pleased to take Śōṉāḍu, I, Kalvāyil
Nāḍāḷvāṉ, also called Kaṇḍaṉ Āvuḍaiyaṉ, made the following endowment
to the Nāyaṇār who abides in Tiruvagattīśvarm temple, in Nelvāyil in
Kalvāyilnāḍu of Kēralasiṅgavaḷanāḍu, on Wednesday the 17 of Vrischikam :-

Whereas, the lands that I endowed for the Periyaṉācciyār(5), the consort of the
Nāyaṇār of Tiruvagattīśvaram in this village, are the Śiṅgaṉātaki vayakkal
lands measuring two varais(6), belonging to Perumāḷ Dēvar, the Kural śey
lands, and the garden that I bought from Aḷagukaṇḍa Pallāvataraiyaṉ,
amounting in all to one mā and a half of iraippaḍi(7) lands;

I, Kalvāyil Nāḍāḷvāṉ, also called Kaṇḍaṉ Āvuḍaiyaṉ, stipulating the
payment of two kalams and a half (of paddy) as irai, which includes
taxes of every description, for every māccēy(8) of land, hereby gave them, with
obḷations of water, to this Periyaṉācciyār Perumāḷ Dēvaṉ and he shall
himself shall pay the taxes in the above manner. May this be under the
protection of all Māhēśvaras."

cells.tamil_fields: header_tamil: மேற்படி கோவில் முன்மண்டபத்திலுள்ள சாசனம்:-
cells.inscription_text:
1. ஸ்வஸ்தி ஸ்ரீ [1*] கொமாறபன்மரான திருபுவனச்சக்கரவர்த்திகள் ஸ்ரீ
2. சத்தாரபாண்டியதெவர்க்கு யாண்டு சவது மிதுனநாயற்று சதுர்த்தியுத்-
3. திக்கள் கிழமையும் பெற்ற உத்திரத்து நாள் கண்டங்
4. உத்தமஞ்செதியான காங்கய கொல்வாய் கங்கநாட்டு
வபனில் இன்னாயினார் விளைகொணுடைய குன்றங்கயத்துக்குறள்
செய்யும் விலித்தெவதானமுத்திரிகவத்திகயக்கும் பாலி-
5. யும் செசெங்கண்ணெனையும் மற்றும் இயைவில் வலளுதபெபுறமும் இவசண்டி
முதல் கடமை அந்தராயம் அச்சாசரி பொன்வரி காடதெய்விகளும்
மற்று எப்பேர்ப்பட்ட சில்வரியினாயத்துக்கு ஈந்திராதித்தவத் செல்-
6. வதாக இக்காசுக்கு இறையிலி காராக்கிழமையாக காடொ[ற்]டிக்கு-
டுதெசென் கண்டம் உத்தமஞ்செதியான காங்கயெநைக் [1*] இவை
காங்கயன் எழுத்து [1*] இது பன்றெழுவனு[சா]தொடுஉ கூ
cells.english_translation:
"Hail! Prosperity! In the fourth year of Tribhuvanaccakravartikal Śrī Sundara Pāṇḍiya Dēvar, also called Kō-Mārapanmar, in the month of Mithuna on the fourth day of the(?)fortnight, a Monday, when the moon was in conjunction with the asterism Uttiram, Gāngēyan, also called Kaṇḍan Udayañjeydān(2), made the following endowment to the Nāyanār of Nelvāy(3):—

Whereas I have, from this year onwards, exempted the lands in Iḷaikkuḍi, which include the Kuṇṛan vayakkal lands, that this Nāyanār bought, the Kuṛaḷ sey lands, the Naḍuvir-dēvadānam lands(4), the Tiruvagattivayal lands, the Pāli lands, the Neḍungaṇṇerai lands(5), besides Nalkuḍai-taḍu-puṛam lands in this hamlet, from the payment of kaḍamai(6), antārāyam(7), accuvāri(8), nāḍenṛavarikal(9) and śilvarikal(10) of every other kind;

I, Gāngēyan, also called Kaṇḍan Udayañjeydān, stipulating that this shall continue for so long as the moon and sun endure, gave these lands to be iraiyili-kāraṇkilamai(11) to this Nāyanār and inscribed the fact on stone.

This is the writing of Gāngēyan. May this be under the protection of all Māhēśvaras."

Footnotes:
[Footnote 1] Nāḍenravari-taxes payable to the nāḍu or district authorities.
[Footnote 2] Iraiyili-kārāṇkilamai-rent-free land with proprietary rights of cultivation and ownership.
[Footnote 3] Śōṉāḍu-koṇḍu-aruḷiya-Śōṉāḍu-Cōla country.
[Footnote 4] Vrischika or Kārttikai, 9th month of the Tamil calendar.
[Footnote 5] Periyaṉācciyār-the name of the Goddess.
[Footnote 6] Varai-land measure.
[Footnote 7] Iraippaḍi-lands paying government tax or irai.
[Footnote 8] Māccēy-a land measure-1 mā of cultivated land.
